## Overview

**Khar'Zul, The Flesh That Remembers** — an Ulrath who rose through centuries of warfare to become one of the Five Great Generals of the Scourge. Unlike many of his fellow commanders, Khar'Zul viewed war as an art to be perfected. His immortality meant that death could not keep him dead — each time his body was destroyed, his essence returned to the Abyss and eventually reformed, carrying with it every memory and lesson from the life he had lived. He was ultimately defeated and sealed within his own greatsword by the First Alliance, becoming the last of three Great Generals to fall.

---

## Species

Ulrath. Among the countless Ulraths that served within the Scourge, only one would rise to become one of the Five Great Generals.

---

## Title

**Khar'Zul, The Flesh That Remembers.** Throughout the centuries of the Scourge War, countless names were given to him by frightened kingdoms and desperate survivors. None endured longer than the one that followed him until his final battle.

---

## Appearance

Khar'Zul towered over nearly every creature that marched beneath the Scourge banner. His immense frame was covered in obsidian-black skin, fractured by rivers of molten fire that pulsed beneath the surface like blood through living veins. Vast horns crowned his head, while great wings of scorched membrane cast shadows over entire battlefields.

Unlike many Ulraths, Khar'Zul carried two legendary weapons into battle: a colossal greatsword — whose name has been lost in history books — forged in the depths of the Abyss, said to be as ancient as the wars themselves; and an abyssal whip of living fire, capable of reducing ranks of soldiers to ash with a single sweep.

---

## Personality

Khar'Zul possessed an intellect that set him apart from nearly every other creature within the Scourge. Where many of its commanders relied upon overwhelming brutality, Khar'Zul viewed war as an art to be perfected. Every campaign, every siege, and every battle became an opportunity to exercise his greatest talent: the calculated destruction of hope.

He rarely raised his voice, rarely acted in anger. His composure never faltered, even amidst the chaos of battle. To those who fought beside him, this calm was often more terrifying than the fury of any beast — for Khar'Zul did not merely seek victory. He sought to ensure that every victory would be remembered and to make sure entire kingdoms were broken long before their armies were defeated. Cities were left standing just long enough for neighboring realms to witness their fall. Survivors were spared not through mercy, but because fear spread farther than fire ever could.

To Khar'Zul, suffering was not an unfortunate consequence of war — it was one of its most effective weapons.

Khar'Zul remained calm even when surrounded by death. Unlike many of the creatures beneath him, he did not need to prove that he was powerful; he already knew that he was. What interested him was understanding: understanding his enemies and allies, understanding fear and suffering, and, above all, understanding how far a creature could be pushed before it broke.

Khar'Zul did not simply enjoy causing pain. He enjoyed designing it. A meaningless slaughter held little interest for him when a carefully constructed sequence of events could cause far greater suffering. A victory was satisfying, but a victory in which the enemy unknowingly walked into a trap that had been prepared for days, months, or even years earlier was something else entirely. It was proof of control.

---

## Philosophy

Khar'Zul believed that existence itself was governed by a single immutable law: **Strength.** To him, mercy, justice, honor, and compassion were temporary illusions created by those incapable of imposing their own will upon the world. Strength was the only truth; everything else merely delayed the inevitable. This belief defined not only how he fought but how he ruled.

Control was what Khar'Zul truly valued. Control over the battlefield, control over his armies, control over his enemies, control over himself. That was why even other creatures of the Scourge feared him.

---

## Military Command

Unlike many of his fellow Generals, Khar'Zul rarely relied on overwhelming numbers alone; he believed victory began long before armies met upon the battlefield. Every campaign was meticulously planned: supply routes were cut, escape paths were eliminated, and cities were isolated before they were besieged. Entire kingdoms often surrendered before Khar'Zul himself ever arrived; those who resisted discovered why his name inspired such fear.

Khar'Zul commanded one of the largest Legions ever assembled by the Scourge. Unlike most Legions, which tended to favor particular species or methods of warfare, his forces were composed of an extraordinary diversity of monstrous races. Each warband retained its own commander, traditions, and methods of combat. Under his command, creatures that should never have been capable of coordinated warfare became devastatingly efficient military forces.

---

## Rise Through the Scourge

### Before the Name

Long before Khar'Zul became one of the Great Generals, he was simply another creature fighting within the endless wars of the Scourge. He was an Ulrath — ancient even by the standards of his kind, possessing the strength, brutality, and destructive nature expected of such a creature. But raw strength was never what separated Khar'Zul from the creatures around him.

He watched. Where other demons saw battlefields, Khar'Zul saw patterns. Where others saw enemies, he saw weaknesses. He learned how different creatures fought, how they reacted to fear, what drove them forward, and what caused them to break. He did not rush into battle simply because he could. He waited, he observed. And when he finally acted, it was usually because he had already considered what would happen several steps ahead.

### The First Gathering

Khar'Zul's rise began when he challenged **Morgath, The Red Maw**, another ancient Ulrath and one of the Scourge's most feared warlords. Morgath was everything the Scourge expected from a demon commander: brutal, overwhelming, and convinced that strength alone was enough to win a war. His armies were infamous for crushing their enemies through sheer force, leaving nothing but ruins behind.

Khar'Zul had watched his campaigns for years. He saw what others did not: Morgath wasted soldiers, resources, and opportunities simply because he possessed the strength to do so. To Khar'Zul, that was not power — it was inefficiency.

The two Ulrath met alone upon a battlefield surrounded by their armies. Morgath expected a contest of strength. Instead, Khar'Zul studied him. Every movement, every attack, every opening was observed and remembered. What appeared to be a desperate struggle was, in truth, Khar'Zul learning exactly how his opponent fought. When Morgath finally committed to a decisive strike, Khar'Zul stepped into the attack and exploited the weakness he had been waiting for. Morgath fell, his torso split from his legs.

By the law of the Gathering, his army became Khar'Zul's spoils. Thousands of creatures now stood before the Ulrath who had defeated their former master — not through strength, but through understanding. That victory marked the beginning of Khar'Zul's rise.

### The Name That Spread

With every victory, Khar'Zul's forces grew. With every defeated warlord, another army was added to his own. Stories began spreading among the Scourge: some claimed he could look at a battlefield and already know where the dead would fall; others spoke of him as an ancient monster who had learned to think like something far more dangerous than a demon.

Eventually, his name became more than the name of a commander. Khar'Zul became a warning. When the battlefield was unusually quiet, commanders wondered whether he was watching. When an enemy's army retreated too easily, they wondered whether it was a trap. When a settlement was spared while everything around it burned, people began asking themselves why — and when the answer was eventually discovered, it was often worse than if Khar'Zul had simply destroyed everything.

### The Mind Behind the Monster

Khar'Zul's intelligence was not a gift he was simply born with — he built it. He studied warfare because he wanted to understand it. He studied his enemies because he wanted to overcome them. He learned to recognize patterns, exploit weaknesses, manipulate the battlefield, and turn even the smallest advantage into victory. Over centuries, that relentless pursuit transformed him into a master tactician.

Where other generals relied on overwhelming power, Khar'Zul learned to make his power meaningful. Where others saw armies, he saw pieces. Where others saw battles, he saw possibilities. And where others relied on instinct, Khar'Zul relied on understanding. He was every bit as powerful as the other Great Generals, but unlike some of them, Khar'Zul did not simply inherit his position through overwhelming natural ability. He earned it.

### The Gathering of Generals

Eventually, Khar'Zul accumulated enough victories that other warlords could no longer ignore him. He had armies large enough to threaten established powers. He had defeated generals who had once been considered untouchable. More importantly, his forces had become frighteningly coordinated under his command. The name of Khar'Zul reached the highest rank of the Scourge, and he was recognized as one of the Five Great Generals — one of the five figures entrusted with commanding vast portions of the Scourge's forces.

---

## Reputation

Among the mortal races, Khar'Zul became the embodiment of the Scourge itself. Cities abandoned their walls upon hearing his Legion had crossed their borders, and entire kingdoms altered military campaigns simply to avoid confronting him. Within the Scourge, however, he inspired something far rarer than fear: respect. Among the Five Great Generals, Khar'Zul earned a reputation unlike any other. He was not regarded as the strongest, nor the most powerful — he was regarded as the most dangerous.

---

## The Flesh That Remembers

Khar'Zul's greatest advantage was not simply his strength, nor his mastery of war. It was the fact that death could not keep him dead. His immortality gave him something few others possessed: time. Whenever his body was destroyed, his essence endured. And when he eventually returned, he carried everything he had learned with him. Every battlefield, every enemy, every mistake, and every victory became another piece of knowledge added to the creature he was becoming.

---

## Fate — The Two Battles

### The First Battle Against Khar'Zul

After felling Voragos and Xerathul, the First Alliance tracked Khar'Zul to a major Scourge stronghold. The Alliance selected a specific group from among its ranks to carry out the attack: Lord Alaric Arkwright, Ragnulf Skallfang, Garrik Thormvuld, Mordrane Vhalor, Soren Kaien, Edmund Drake, and Cassian Aurelius. They were entrusted with bringing down Khar'Zul.

The battle was unlike anything they had anticipated. Khar'Zul was not merely a monster surrounded by an army — he commanded the battlefield himself, constantly adapting to the Alliance's strategies and exploiting weaknesses within their formation. The Alliance suffered devastating losses, including the death of two of the heroes: Soren Kaien and Edmund Drake. Yet for the first time, Khar'Zul found himself facing opponents who could match him not only in strength, but in coordination. Eventually, after an immense struggle and countless losses, the ancient Ulrath was defeated. Khar'Zul fell.

### The First Return

The Alliance had done what no army before them had managed to accomplish — the ancient Ulrath lay motionless among the ruins, his massive form reduced to ash and burning fragments. Then something went wrong. The remains of Khar'Zul did not simply fade. The ash began to move against the wind. Blackened fragments of flesh lifted from the ground and spiraled toward the place where his body had fallen. The air around the battlefield grew unnaturally hot, while the ground beneath the ruins began to crack with faint crimson light. The remains were drawn together into a swirling mass of smoke, blood, and infernal energy — and then they were gone. Not destroyed. Taken.

For a few moments, nothing happened. Then, from somewhere far beyond the battlefield, a deep infernal roar echoed through the air. What the Alliance had witnessed was the remains of his physical form being pulled back toward the Abyss, where his essence would endure until it could once again manifest in a body. Their victory had lasted only moments. They had killed Khar'Zul, but they had not ended him. When the Alliance eventually learned that Khar'Zul had returned to the world, the truth became impossible to ignore: Khar'Zul was immortal.

### The Birth of the Sealing Ritual

The discovery forced the Alliance to confront a problem none of them had anticipated. If Khar'Zul's essence could survive the destruction of his body, then defeating him again would only delay his return. They needed to find a way to contain the essence itself.

Their search eventually led them to an unlikely possibility: Khar'Zul's sword. It had been at his side throughout centuries of warfare, crossing battlefields with him, surviving his conquests, and serving as the instrument through which countless lives had been taken. It was not magically bound to him, but it had endured centuries of exposure to his power, his violence, and the evil carried through his reign.

Mordrane Vhalor and his followers theorized that such an object might possess the strength necessary to withstand an essence as powerful as Khar'Zul's — not because it belonged to him, but because nothing else had endured Khar'Zul for so long. The theory was considered dangerous, perhaps even impossible, but after witnessing Khar'Zul return from death, the Alliance could no longer afford to dismiss impossible ideas. And so, the foundation of the sealing ritual was born.

### The Final Battle Against Khar'Zul

The Alliance confronted Khar'Zul once more. This time, they came prepared. The battle became a war within a war — while the armies of the Last Stand fought to prevent the Scourge from overwhelming them, the heroes fought directly against Khar'Zul. He was stronger than before: smarter, more cautious. He understood many of their methods because he had already fought them once. The Alliance understood this as well. The battle became a contest between Khar'Zul's centuries of experience and the combined knowledge of those who had spent years preparing specifically for this moment.

Eventually, the Alliance managed to bring him down once more. But this time, they were ready. The moment Khar'Zul's physical form began to collapse, Garrik Thormvuld's devices activated, anchoring the surrounding energy and preventing the essence from escaping, allowing Mordrane Vhalor to begin the ritual.

Khar'Zul's essence resisted. The sword itself began to react as the ancient power of its master was drawn toward it. The Alliance fought to maintain the ritual while Khar'Zul fought to break free. The sword became the center of the battlefield, and when the ritual reached its climax, the essence of Khar'Zul was finally dragged into the weapon that had once belonged to him. The sealing was successful. He had become imprisoned within it.

### The Fate of the Sword

After the battle, the sword was not destroyed — that was impossible. It had now become the prison containing Khar'Zul's essence, and destroying the weapon risked releasing the very thing the Alliance had sacrificed so much to contain. Instead, the sword was placed somewhere specifically constructed to keep it isolated from the world. A heavily guarded vault was established under the protection of the Last Stand, with Thormvuld technology and magical wards designed to prevent the sword from being accessed or transported without the knowledge of the Alliance's remaining guardians. For generations, the sword remained there — hidden, guarded, forgotten by most of the world. But not everyone.
